order: Build the dispatch layer over the existing registry as a router module at the repo root. Transcribe the plan's casting tables into a single data file. It must list rungs, roles, the hard never-rules, the computed review matrix, the degradation ladder, and the automatic-trigger rules, and the router reads it rather than hardcoding them; check every rung against an independent transcription of the source table in both directions. The route function fails closed on any ownership-invariant violation, resolving a role only through a loaded, intact registry. Reviewer selection computes no-self-family status from the full co-author set, and unattributed or mixed-family authorship fails closed rather than dispatching open. A missing required companion task blocks the dispatch entirely, and nothing proceeds until every required companion exists. Mark any default the plan leaves silent as an explicit unstated choice rather than guessing. Wire the new suite into CI and keep the gate-class order — cross-vendor review before merge — unchanged.
claims: 74 checks went green, including an exhaustive sweep across every bucket-state combination confirming no mandatory-class dispatch ever produces a same-family closing verdict — every non-close case typed DOES_NOT_CLOSE. No-self-family behavior was checked for every author-family combination, and an independent bidirectional transcription check confirmed every rung matches the source table. Fail-closed loading was tamper-tested against registry corruption, never-rule violations, vendor/family mismatches, and off-ladder inputs; CI runs the suite.
